sources.title: INALI: Norma de escritura de la lengua Hñähñu
sources.note: Original indexed introduction: internal diversity, regional names, tone and nasal vowels. No dated population statistics used.

sources.title: INAH: Huamango
sources.note: Original indexed complete site description: artificial terraces, residential platforms and defensive walls. INAH identifies settlement as Otomian.

sources.title: INAH: Zona Arqueológica de Huamango
sources.note: Original indexed full text: occupation 900 to 1300, tentative subdivisions and ceramic comparisons. No unsupported ethnic attribution to earlier Teotihuacan.

sources.title: INAH: Códice Huamantla
sources.note: Original institutional catalogue: sixteenth-century amate pictorial account of migration, fighting and Spanish-era church. Fragment counts differ from technical article, so count and largest-in-world superlative omitted.

sources.title: Alejandro Huerta and Eugenia Berthier: Códice de Huamantla, investigación de materiales originales
sources.note: Original indexed primary conservation study; section Color rojo identifies cochineal in two samples; water-based binder possibly tzacutli remains tentative and is not asserted. Article predates online upload date, no publication year assigned.

sources.title: INPI: Otomíes, Etnografía
sources.note: Original indexed Historia and Organización social. Local variation explicitly acknowledged; rigid timeless gender roles not copied.

sources.title: Patricia Fournier García: De la Teotlalpan al valle del Mezquital
sources.note: Original article and same-issue indexed PDF checked; printed page 189 on agave fibre, fermented sap, pottery and dispersed settlement. Do not separately count issue download as another work.

sources.title: UNESCO: Otomí-Chichimeca places of memory and living traditions of Tolimán
sources.note: Original full indexed nomination summary, inscription 2009. Local practices of Tolimán, not all Otomí communities.

sources.title: Ana María Crespo and Beatriz Cervantes: Raíz colonial de la tradición otomiana (1990)
sources.note: Direct original abstract and indexed original PDF /14614/15683 checked. Scope Guanajuato to Querétaro including Sierra Gorda foothills, colonial movement and settlement.

sources.title: INAH: San Luis Huamantla
sources.note: Original indexed historical section: Otomí defenders of Tlaxcalan frontier at Tecoac in 1519, then churches and colonial settlement.

sources.title: INALI: Hñähñu courtesy phrases, voice by Nicandro González Peña
sources.note: Direct phrase list and full indexed introduction checked: specifically Valle del Mezquital; Ki hats'i / Buenos días (saludo común). Modern Latin-letter writing.

sources.title: INALI: Participants in the Hñähñu writing standard
sources.note: Original full indexed list and introduction; community representatives, educators, language activists, Academy and researchers.

sources.title: INALI: Lengua Tének (huasteco)
sources.note: Direct institutional page; body dated 20 December 2024 despite title suffix 2025. Mayan language family and communities of San Luis Potosí and Veracruz. No old population number presented as current.

sources.title: INPI: Huastecos, Etnografía
sources.note: Direct fetch timed out; full original indexed text checked using site.atlas.inpi.gob.mx/huastecos-etnografia zacahuil. Sections Historia, Organización social and Gastronomía. Mexica endpoint 1506 not adopted; no single date asserted for all Spanish conquest.

sources.title: INAH: Las Flores
sources.note: Direct institutional site description: mound A, 26 floors, dimensions and lime/crushed-shell technique. Site phases are approximate and no construction midpoint year is invented.

sources.title: INAH: Tamohí (El Consuelo)
sources.note: Direct institutional description: river setting, cotton and food crops, altar interior and painted figures. Abandonment chronology differs between INAH pages, so exact founding/abandonment dates are not adopted.

sources.title: Laura del Olmo Frese, Museo Nacional de Antropología: Adolescente huasteco
sources.note: Direct June 2020 museum object essay. Inventory 03.0-00588, sandstone, height 145 cm, Tamohi West Structure; competing iconographic interpretations preserved as interpretations.

sources.title: Estela Martínez Mora, INAH: La antigua ciudad de Tamtoc
sources.note: Direct article by INAH investigator. Water channels and deposits; residential complex excavated in 2015 belongs to 450 to 900 period, specialist craft-house attribution explicitly tentative. Older institutional origin dates differ; no exact founding year adopted.

sources.title: INALI: Tének courtesy phrases
sources.note: Direct phrase list and introduction: western Tének of San Luis Potosí, text and voices by Luis Flores Martínez and Esiquio Martínez Cruz; Nenek / Hola. Modern written language, not a preconquest inscription.

sources.title: INALI: El Principito in Tének, 26 September 2016
sources.note: Direct original press release and date. Telésforo del Ángel Domínguez is identified as a community speaker and language promoter; article does not explicitly identify him as translator, so that role is not assigned.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Proposed shared peoples narrative, not a unified-state equivalence. Broad preconquest snapshot and narrow colonial northern phase explicitly distinguished in opening, periods and source-specific passage.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: hnahnu-otomi 1492 to 1500 bbox [-100.9936,18.8288,-97.3972,21.5578]; otomies index1530 to 1650, first world-1530 feature1530 to 1600 bbox [-100.4752,21.0875,-99.5140,21.9424]. Later record lies in northern Querétaro/Guanajuato to Sierra Gorda region. No assertion of exact ethnic frontier.
batchIdentityNotes.associationEvidence: Crespo/Cervantes 1990 specifically studies Otomí-speaking colonial settlement in Guanajuato/Querétaro and Sierra Gorda foothills; INALI documents regional linguistic diversity. No Pame or Jonaz IDs absorbed. Root may decline the additional association without losing the main narrative.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Modern Mezquital Hñähñu greeting specifically attributed; no universal Otomí spelling or ancient inscription claimed.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Living Teenek peoples and specifically attributed Huastec regional archaeology; no claim all Huasteca residents were Teenek or formed one state.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: world-1492 first feature 1492 to 1500, bbox [-99.4347943,21.2287359,-97.5303753,23.0425427]. Outline covers part of the northeastern Mexican Huasteca, not the full historical region or contemporary communities. Original dates retained as map coverage.
batchIdentityNotes.chronology: Older and newer INAH Tamtoc starting dates differ; broad earlier urban context retained without invented founding date. Tamohi pages conflict on abandonment century; exact endpoint omitted. Writing is specifically modern western Tének and not a deciphered preconquest inscription.
batchIdentityNotes.sourceAccess: Eight institutional pages; INPI ethnography available as full indexed original despite direct timeout. Other key object, water, phrase and publishing pages read directly.
